Rashi on Megillah 10b:13:1.hebrew: אמוץ ואמציה - אמוץ אביו של ישעיה, ואמציה מלך יהודה:
Rashi on Megillah 10b:13:1.english: Amoz and Amaziah - Amoz [was] the father of Isaiah, and Amaziah [was] king of Judah:

Rashi on Megillah 10b:15:1.hebrew: מלמד שכיסתה פניה בבית חמיה - לפיכך לא הכירה עכשיו, שאף בביתו לא ראה פניה שיהא מכירה:
Rashi on Megillah 10b:15:1.english: This teaches that she covered her face in her father-in-law's house - Therefore, he did not recognize her now, because even in his house he had not seen her face [such] that he would recognize her:

Rashi on Megillah 10b:16:1.hebrew: אינו מן המדה - אינו אוחז למעט מדת קרקע לכל צדדיו כלום, כדקתני: "יש לו עשר אמות לכל רוח" — באמצע בית קדש הקדשים היה יושב, ויש ריוח בינו לבין הכתלים עשר אמות לכל צד, וכל הבית אינו אלא כ' על כ', נמצא שאינו ממעט כלום:
Rashi on Megillah 10b:16:1.english: Is not [included] in the measurement - It does not occupy [any space] so as to diminish the measurement of the floor space on any of its sides at all, as it is taught: "It has ten cubits on every side" — [for the Ark] was situated in the middle of the chamber of the Holy of Holies, and there was a space of ten cubits between it and the walls on every side, while the entire chamber is only twenty [cubits] by twenty [cubits]; thus, it follows that it does not diminish [the space] at all:

Rashi on Megillah 10b:17:1.hebrew: לפני הדביר - חלל בית קדש הקדשים שהוא לפנים; הדביר היא המחיצה המבדלת בין הקדש ובין קדש הקדשים:
Rashi on Megillah 10b:17:1.english: Before the devir - [This refers to] the space of the Holy of Holies, which is within; the devir is the partition that separates between the Sanctuary and the Holy of Holies:

Rashi on Megillah 10b:18:1.hebrew: פתח לה פיתחא להאי פרשתא מהכא - כשהיה רוצה לדרוש בענין איגרת פורים, היה מתחיל לדרוש מקרא זה:
Rashi on Megillah 10b:18:1.english: [He] introduced this passage with an introduction from here - When [he] wanted to expound upon the matter of the letter of Purim [the Book of Esther], he would begin by expounding this verse:

Rashi on Megillah 10b:18:2.english: For I will rise up against them - [This] is written regarding the punishment of Babylonia:

Rashi on Megillah 10b:18:3.hebrew: זה הכתב - אין להן כתב, אלא מאומה אחרת:
Rashi on Megillah 10b:18:3.english: This is the writing - They have no writing [of their own], except from another nation:

Rashi on Megillah 10b:18:4.hebrew: נין - לשון ממשלה, וכן "ינון שמו" (תהילים ע״ב:י״ז) — ימשול ויגדל:
Rashi on Megillah 10b:18:4.english: Offspring [nin] - An expression [denoting] dominion; and similarly, "May his name endure [yinon]" (Psalms 72:17) — [meaning] he will rule and grow great.

Rashi on Megillah 10b:1:1.hebrew: הא אמרי - לקמן בסיפא דהא מתני' גופה קאמרי דלא צריכי לקדושי, דקא מסיים ואזיל בה: "וכל שתעלה בידך מסורת מאבותיך":
Rashi on Megillah 10b:1:1.english: Didn't they say - Later, at the end of this very baraita itself, [they say] that they do not need to be consecrated, as it goes on to conclude in it: "And whatever comes into your hand as a tradition from your ancestors":

Rashi on Megillah 10b:25:1.hebrew: בצאת לפני החלוץ - ביהושפט כתיב בדברי הימים, כשיצא להלחם על העמונים והגבעונים שבאו עליו:
Rashi on Megillah 10b:25:1.english: As they went out before the army - [This] is written regarding Jehoshaphat in Chronicles, when he went out to fight against the Ammonites and the Gibeonites who came against him:

Rashi on Megillah 10b:25:2.english: Give thanks to the Lord, for [He is] good - [This] implies [that it is] good that they should offer praise before Him for this:

Rashi on Megillah 10b:27:1.english: [He] causes others to rejoice - And when [Israel] became liable for destruction in the days of Haman, their enemies rejoiced over them:

Rashi on Megillah 10b:29:1.hebrew: ושמתי כסאי בעילם - שושן הבירה היתה בעילם, דכתיב בספר דניאל: "בשושן הבירה אשר בעילם המדינה":
Rashi on Megillah 10b:29:1.english: And I will set my throne in Elam - Shushan the capital was in Elam, as it is written in the Book of Daniel: "In Shushan the capital, which is in the province of Elam":

Rashi on Megillah 10b:2:1.hebrew: כל המצות הללו - הנוהגות בערי חומה: שילוח מצורע, וקריאת מגילה בחמשה עשר, והבית חלוט בה לסוף שנה:
Rashi on Megillah 10b:2:1.english: All these mitzvot - [namely, those] that apply in walled cities: sending out a metzora, reading the Megillah on the fifteenth [of Adar], and [that] a house [sold] in it becomes permanently transferred [to the buyer] at the end of a year:

Rashi on Megillah 10b:3:1.hebrew: אע"פ שאין כו' - אלמא סבירא ליה קדושה קמייתא לא בטלה מחמת חורבן, והיינו תנאי:
Rashi on Megillah 10b:3:1.english: Even though it does not [have a wall now], etc. - Thus he [Rabbi Elazar bar Yosei] holds that the first consecration was not nullified because of the destruction, and this is [a dispute between] Tannaim:

Rashi on Megillah 10b:6:1.hebrew: וחרבו שלופה וגו' - וציערו, שהוכיחו על ביטול תורה ותמיד של בין הערבים, כדאמר לעיל בפירקין (מגילה ג.):
Rashi on Megillah 10b:6:1.english: With his sword drawn, etc. - And [the angel] distressed him, for he rebuked him concerning the neglect of Torah [study] and the afternoon daily [tamid] offering, as was stated earlier in our chapter (Megillah 3a):

Rashi on Megillah 10b:7:1.hebrew: ויהי דוד לכל דרכיו משכיל וה' עמו - וכתיב התם "ויהי שאול עוין את דוד", בשביל הצלחתו:
Rashi on Megillah 10b:7:1.english: And David was successful in all his ways, and the Lord was with him - And it is written there, "And Saul eyed David" [with suspicion], because of his success:

Tosafot on Megillah 10b:18:1.hebrew: שאר זה לשון - קשה, שעדיין הם מספרין [בבבל] בלשון ארמית; ונראה דרוצה לומר [לשון מלכות] שהמלכים משתמשין בו, שאין שאר [העם] מכירין בו:
Tosafot on Megillah 10b:18:1.english: “Remnant,” this is language - [This is] difficult, for they still speak in Babylonia in the Aramaic language; and it seems that [the Gemara] means to say a royal language that the kings use, which the rest of the people are not familiar with:

Tosafot on Megillah 10b:29:1.hebrew: רבה בר עופרן - גרסינן, ולא גרסינן "עפרון", ד"שם רשעים ירקב", ולא מסקו בשמייהו:
Tosafot on Megillah 10b:29:1.english: Rabba bar Oferan - [This is what] we read, and we do not read "Efron," because "the name of the wicked shall rot," and they do not name [people] by their names:
